simple: `nil` means nothing at all, like an empty box. You can set a variable or table entry to `nil` to clear it. Setting a part's `Parent` to `nil` takes it out of the game world, and you can put it back later. When nothing in your scripts points to something anymore, Luau cleans it up to free memory.
analogy: `nil` is like an empty parking space. The space exists, but there is no car in it. Setting something to `nil` is like driving the car away.
keyPoints: `nil` means non-existence or nothingness. It is not the same as `0`, `false`, or an empty string.
Only `nil` and `false` count as false in an `if` check. Everything else counts as true.
Set a variable to `nil` to clear it, like `score = nil`.
Set a table key to `nil` to remove it, like `days.Tuesday = nil`.
Setting a part's `Parent` to `nil` removes it from view, but it still exists if a variable still points to it.
You can bring it back by setting `Parent` again, like `part.Parent = workspace`.
The garbage collector deletes data no script can reach anymore. Setting big unused variables to `nil` helps it.

terms.nil: The value that means "nothing here". Reading a variable that was never set gives `nil`.
terms.evaluate to true: What a value counts as in an `if` check. `5` counts as true; `nil` counts as false.
terms.garbage collector: Luau's automatic cleaner. It deletes values that no script can reach anymore, to free memory.
terms.reference: A variable that points to a value or object. While a reference exists, the object is kept.
terms.Parent: The object something sits inside in the Explorer. A part with Parent `nil` is not in the game world.
terms.memory: The space the computer uses to hold your game's data while it runs.

example.title: Hide a part and bring it back
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
part.Parent = Workspace -- now you can see it

task.wait(2)
part.Parent = nil -- gone from the world, but the variable still holds it

task.wait(2)
part.Parent = Workspace -- it comes back

task.wait(2)
part.Parent = nil
part = nil -- no more references, so the garbage collector can delete it
explain: The script makes a part and puts it in Workspace so you can see it.
After 2 seconds, setting `Parent` to `nil` removes it from the world.
Because the variable `part` still points to it, you can bring it back by setting `Parent` again.
At the end, setting both `Parent` and `part` to `nil` lets Luau clean it up.

watchOut: Thinking `0` or `""` is like `nil`. In Luau they both count as true.
Using a value that might be `nil`, like `part.Name` when `part` is `nil`. That causes an error, so check `if part then` first.
Thinking `Parent = nil` deletes an object forever. It just removes it from the world; use `:Destroy()` to really get rid of it.
